card.name: Verbs after 'can' in warning statements
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of warning sentences just before the main outcome, mostly the verb after 'can' or 'may' (occur, lead, contribute) in NSAID and opioid warnings. Also fires on 'factors' in 'risk factors' and 'such' before 'patients'.

modes.label: Verb after can/may
modes.description: The verb right after 'can' or 'may' that introduces an adverse effect in a warnings section.
modes.example: Respiratory depression can<< occur>> at any time during opioid therapy, especially

modes.label: Linking word in risk phrase
modes.description: A noun or determiner just before the outcome or population, such as 'factors' or 'such'.
modes.example: patients with known CV disease or risk<< factors>> had a higher absolute incidence of excess serious

modes.label: Code sentence end
modes.description: A period ending a code comment before the next statement in programming text.
modes.example: CWnd wnd; // Create a window object<<. >>wnd.CreateWindow(...); // Create the
